title: React Accessibility Applied Check
description: Apply accessibility knowledge to edge cases involving ARIA, keyboard interaction, forms, focus management, and testing.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt:
A custom clickable card uses `
Buy
` and cannot be activated with Enter or Space. What is the best fix?

options.text: Use a native button for the action or fully implement button semantics and keyboard behavior

questions.explanation: Native buttons are the right default for actions because they include keyboard and semantic behavior.

questions.prompt: An icon-only close button has no text label. What should you add?
questions.explanation: Icon-only controls need a programmatic label because the icon may not provide a useful name.

questions.prompt: A modal opens but focus stays behind it on the page. What is the accessibility problem?

options.text: Keyboard users may interact with background content and miss the dialog

questions.explanation: Dialogs need deliberate focus management so keyboard and assistive technology users enter and leave predictably.

questions.prompt: A form submit fails validation. Which improvements help accessibility? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Associate each error with its field
Use color alone to mark invalid fields
Move focus or announce the error state appropriately

questions.explanation: Validation should be perceivable, associated with fields, and reachable without relying only on color.

questions.prompt: A disabled-looking submit button is actually a styled link with `href="#"`. What is the problem?

options.text: The element role and behavior do not match the intended action

questions.explanation: Choose elements by meaning: links navigate, buttons perform actions.

questions.prompt: A status message appears after async save but screen reader users get no feedback. What pattern can help?

options.text: A polite live region for non-disruptive status updates
Removing the message from the DOM

questions.explanation: Live regions can announce dynamic save, loading, or error messages.

questions.prompt: A developer adds `role="button"` to a `<div>` and assumes accessibility is complete. What is missing?

options.text: Keyboard handling, focusability, states, and expected behavior

questions.explanation: ARIA roles do not add native keyboard behavior or manage focus by themselves.

questions.prompt: Your automated axe test passes, but Tab navigation skips the primary menu. What should you conclude?

options.text: Manual keyboard testing still found a real issue to fix
The issue is impossible because automation passed
Only source maps can diagnose it

questions.explanation: Automated checks complement manual testing; passing automation does not prove every interaction works.
